title: Graded Hilbert syzygy for a polynomial ring in any finite number of variables
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $m\geq0$ be an integer, and let $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with $S_a$ the $k$-span of monomials of total degree $a$ for $a\geq0$ and $S_a=0$ for $a<0$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathbf Z}M_b$ be a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $S_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$. For an integer $d$, define the graded shift by $S(d)_b=S_{d+b}$. There exist finite sets $I_0,\ldots,I_m$, integers $d_{j,r}$ for $r\in I_j$, and degree-preserving $S$-linear maps forming an exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow F_m\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0,\qquad F_j=\bigoplus_{r\in I_j}S(d_{j,r}).$$
Exactness means injectivity at the left end, surjectivity onto $M$, and equality of each image with the next kernel. Empty sets, $M=0$, arbitrary integer generator degrees, and $m=0$ (so $S=k$ and $F_0\to M$ is an isomorphism) are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), global dimension m, together with Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), finite homogeneous generation and graded Nakayama. The degree-preserving finite shifted-free enhancement is an agent-extracted algebraic consequence of these results, not the literal statement of 00OQ.

proof.text: For any finite graded $S$-module $N$, take finite generators and replace each by its finitely many homogeneous components. The resulting finite family $n_r\in N_{e_r}$ generates $N$: the span contains every original generator, while all the components are themselves in $N$. Put $C(N)=\bigoplus_r S(-e_r)$ and send its r-th basis vector to $n_r$. This map is surjective by generation. Its basis vector has degree $e_r$ since $S(-e_r)_b=S_{b-e_r}$; multiplication therefore shows that the map preserves degree.

source.place: Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), proof: replacement by homogeneous generators and the map in part (4).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $S$ is Noetherian. Set $K_0=M$. For $0\leq j<m$, assuming $K_j$ finite and graded, use step 1 to choose $q_j:F_j=C(K_j)\twoheadrightarrow K_j$ and set $K_{j+1}=\ker q_j$. This kernel is graded: applying $q_j$ to the homogeneous decomposition of an element gives zero in each distinct degree, so every component is again in the kernel. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], since $F_j$ has a finite basis. This proves the induction, starting from the given finite $M$. Composing $q_j$ with $K_j\hookrightarrow F_{j-1}$ for $j\geq1$ gives an exact partial resolution $0\to K_m\to F_{m-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to0$ when $m>0$. Every $F_j$ is projective: in the direct-summand characterization its underlying free module is a summand of itself by the identity maps.

source.place: Tags 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), first sentence, and 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), submodule assertion; explicit graded free-cover induction.

proof.text: [lem-sfb-polynomial-projective-dimension-bound] supplies a projective resolution of $M$ of length at most $m$. For $m>0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-kernel-projective] with $d=m$ to the partial resolution of step 2: all its $F_j$ are projective, so its leftmost kernel $K_m$ is projective. For $m=0$ use the same node's length-zero assertion to see that $K_0=M$ is projective; no partial resolution is needed.

source.place: Tags 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), global dimension bound, and 00O5 (lemma-independent-resolution), terminal-kernel assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-connected-graded-projective-free] to $A=S$ and $P=K_m$: the total-degree grading is nonnegative, its degree-zero part is $k$, and steps 2 and 3 give finite generation and ungraded projectivity. Let $F_m=\bigoplus_r S(-e_r)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_m$ be its degree-preserving isomorphism. For $m>0$ compose with the inclusion $K_m\hookrightarrow F_{m-1}$. The composition is injective and its image is exactly the kernel at $F_{m-1}$; every other image-kernel equality and the augmentation surjectivity are inherited from step 2. For $m=0$ the isomorphism $F_0\cong K_0=M$ itself is the augmentation. Put $d_{j,r}=-e_{j,r}$ for every chosen basis degree. These are precisely the requested shifts and degree-preserving maps.

source.place: Tag 0EKB (lemma-graded-NAK), homogeneous-basis consequence isolated in lem-sfb-connected-graded-projective-free; splicing by the kernel inclusion.

proof.text: If $M=0$, choose every $I_j$ empty and every map zero; the sequence is exact. If an intermediate $K_j$ vanishes, choose its cover zero and all later kernels and covers zero. Negative generator degrees are allowed throughout because the shifts use all integers. Thus neither a nonzero module nor a nonempty basis nor a positive number of variables was assumed.
